legend: Medium magnification shows monotonous epithelial cells with low-grade nuclei in the left portion of the papillary lesion. On the basis of cytology, architecture, and size (> 3 mm), this lesion is diagnosed as intraductal papilloma with ductal carcinoma in situ.

legend: CK5 is negative in ductal carcinoma in situ (left) and highlights the myoepithelial cells lining the fibrovascular cores in both portions of the papilloma. The benign epithelium is also negative for CK5 in this case, as the epithelium is apocrine and columnar. CK5 is typically positive in usual ductal hyperplasia lining papillomas.
Ultrasonography shows a markedly cystic dilated duct containing a large intraductal papilloma.

legend: Intraductal papilloma with usual ductal hyperplasia, surrounding fibrosis and a core biopsy tract. Epithelial displacement is noted.

diagnosis: Intraductal papilloma with florid usual ductal hyperplasia and focal atypical apocrine ductal hyperplasia.
legend: Vacuum assisted breast core biopsies show an intraductal papillary lesion composed of arborescent to anastomosing fronds supported by fibrous and oedematous fibrovascular cores accompanied by florid usual ductal hyperplasia and focal apocrine metaplasia. Focal luminal mucin is noted among the apocrine population. Part of the apocrine proliferation shows well-defined luminal spaces reflecting architectural atypia and in keeping with focal atypical apocrine ductal hyperplasia. No malignancy is present.
